content:
# Sirach 25 — Disagreement Log
**Chapter:** Sirach 25 | **Date:** 2026-03-17 | **Total Disagreements:** 14

---

## Disagreement 001 — 25:1 "I was made beautiful / I find beauty"
**Verse:** 25:1
**EMET:** "In-three-things I-was-made-beautiful"
**LOGOS:** "In three things I find beauty"
**PNEUMA:** "Three things fill me with delight"
**Issue:** ἐκαλλιώθην — aorist passive "I was made beautiful/adorned." EMET preserves the passive precisely. LOGOS's "I find beauty" shifts to active and present. PNEUMA's "fill me with delight" is a further interpretive departure. The aorist passive matters: beauty is something that happened to the speaker.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "In three things I find beauty" — active is more natural; the aorist passive is noted.

---

## Disagreement 002 — 25:2 "rich-man-of-falsehood / rich man who lies"
**Verse:** 25:2
**EMET:** "a-rich-man-of-falsehood"
**LOGOS:** "a rich man who lies"
**PNEUMA:** "a dishonest rich person"
**Issue:** πλούσιον ψεύστην — "a lying rich man." EMET's genitive construction is literal; LOGOS and PNEUMA are both acceptable. SOPHIA uses "deceitful" for "ψεύστην" as slightly broader than "lies."
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "a wealthy man who is deceitful."

---

## Disagreement 003 — 25:3 rhetorical question form
**Verse:** 25:3
**EMET:** "In-your-youth you-did-not-gather — and how-will-you-find in-your-old-age?"
**LOGOS:** "If you did not gather wisdom in your youth, how will you find it in your old age?"
**PNEUMA:** "If you didn't build up wisdom when you were young, what will you have to draw on when you're old?"
**Issue:** The Greek is a direct statement + rhetorical question; LOGOS and PNEUMA convert to conditional. EMET preserves the blunter two-part structure. Both are defensible.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "If you did not gather wisdom in your youth, how will you find it in your old age?" — LOGOS form is standard.

---

## Disagreement 004 — 25:6 "experience / crown / glory"
**Verse:** 25:6
**EMET:** "A-great-thing is the-experience of-the-elders, and a-crown of-glory is the-fear of-the-LORD"
**LOGOS:** "Experience is the crown of the elders, and the fear of the LORD is their glory"
**PNEUMA:** "Experience is the elders' crown; the fear of the LORD is their glory"
**Issue:** The Greek has two parallel nominative predicates. EMET takes "experience" as the subject and makes "crown" secondary; LOGOS and PNEUMA reorganize to make "experience" the "crown." Both readings are supported. SOPHIA follows LOGOS for its cleaner parallelism.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "Experience is the crown of the elders, and their glory is the fear of the LORD."

---

## Disagreement 005 — 25:11 "surpasses all-else / surpasses everything / beats everything"
**Verse:** 25:11
**EMET:** "The-fear of-the-LORD surpasses all-else"
**LOGOS:** "The fear of the LORD surpasses everything"
**PNEUMA:** "The fear of the LORD beats everything"
**Issue:** πάντα ὑπεράγει — "surpasses/exceeds everything." "Beats" (PNEUMA) is colloquial. "Surpasses" is the standard English rendering. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "The fear of the LORD surpasses everything."

---

## Disagreement 006 — 25:13 "Any-wound / Any wound" and the woman
**Verse:** 25:13
**EMET/LOGOS:** "Any wound but not the wound of the heart! Any evil but not the evil of a woman!"
**PNEUMA:** "Any wound — but not the wound of the heart! Any pain — but not the pain caused by a woman!"
**Issue:** πάσῃ πληγῇ — "any blow/wound." PNEUMA substitutes "pain" for the second "evil" instance. The Greek parallelism has πονηρία γυναικός — "wickedness/evil of a woman," not simply pain. SOPHIA preserves "evil" as theologically weighted.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "Any wound — but not a wound of the heart! Any evil — but not the evil caused by a woman!"

---

## Disagreement 007 — 25:15 "head of a serpent" comparison
**Verse:** 25:15
**EMET:** "There-is-no-head above the-head of a-serpent"
**LOGOS:** "There is no head more poisonous than the head of a serpent"
**PNEUMA:** "No head strikes more lethally than a serpent's head"
**Issue:** οὐκ ἔστιν κεφαλὴ ὑπὲρ κεφαλὴν ὄφεως — "there is no head above the head of a serpent." The point is supremacy of the serpent's head (most deadly). EMET is literal; LOGOS adds "poisonous" (interpretive); PNEUMA adds "strikes lethally" (very interpretive). SOPHIA retains "more deadly."
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "There is no head more deadly than the head of a serpent."

---

## Disagreement 008 — 25:16 "evil-woman / wicked woman / vicious woman"
**Verse:** 25:16
**EMET:** "an-evil-woman"
**LOGOS:** "a wicked woman"
**PNEUMA:** "a vicious woman"
**Issue:** γυναικὸς πονηρᾶς — "an evil/wicked woman." "Vicious" (PNEUMA) is stronger than the Greek warrants. "Wicked" (LOGOS) is standard for πονηρός.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "a wicked woman."

---

## Disagreement 009 — 25:17 "darkens her face like a bear's"
**Verse:** 25:17
**EMET:** "she-darkens her-face like a-bear's"
**LOGOS:** "darkens her expression like a bear's"
**PNEUMA:** "she goes around scowling like a bear"
**Issue:** ἀρκτοῦ — "bear." PNEUMA's "scowling" adds an interpretation. The Greek says she blackens/darkens her face like a bear's face. SOPHIA: "darkens her expression like a bear's."
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "and darkens her expression like a bear's."

---

## Disagreement 010 — 25:20 "garrulous-wife / garrulous wife / nagging wife"
**Verse:** 25:20
**EMET:** "a-garrulous-wife to a-quiet-man"
**LOGOS:** "a garrulous wife to a quiet man"
**PNEUMA:** "a nagging wife to a peaceful man"
**Issue:** γυναικὸς γλωσσώδους — "a talkative/gossipy/garrulous woman." PNEUMA's "nagging" adds a negative behavioral descriptor not fully in the Greek. "Garrulous" is accurate.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "a garrulous wife to a quiet man."

---

## Disagreement 011 — 25:22 interpretation of wife as provider
**Verse:** 25:22
**EMET:** "Anger and insolence and great-shame [it-is when] a-wife provides-for her-husband"
**LOGOS:** "Anger and shamelessness and great disgrace — when a wife supports her husband"
**PNEUMA:** "Rage, shamelessness, utter humiliation — that's what it means for a wife to be the one keeping the household going"
**Issue:** The Greek reflects the ancient assumption that a wife providing for a husband is shameful (reversal of roles). All agents preserve this honestly. PNEUMA adds "keeping the household going" as explanation. SOPHIA retains the compact form.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "Rage and shamelessness and great disgrace — when a wife supports her husband."

---

## Disagreement 012 — 25:24 "from a woman the beginning of sin"
**Verse:** 25:24
**EMET:** "From a-woman the-beginning of-sin, and because-of-her we-all-die"
**LOGOS:** "From a woman came the beginning of sin, and because of her we all die"
**PNEUMA:** "Sin entered the world through a woman, and because of her we all die"
**Issue:** ἀπὸ γυναικὸς ἀρχὴ ἁμαρτίας — "from a woman the beginning of sin." This is Ben Sira's interpretation of Gen 3, and a notably misogynistic one in context (contra the broader Hebrew tradition which distributes blame or focuses on Adam). PNEUMA's "entered the world" echoes Romans 5:12 but is not in the Greek. SOPHIA renders literally.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "From a woman came the beginning of sin, and because of her we all die."

---

## Disagreement 013 — 25:25 "permission to spread-herself / free rein"
**Verse:** 25:25
**EMET:** "to an-evil-wife permission to-spread-herself"
**LOGOS:** "do not give a wicked wife free rein"
**PNEUMA:** "don't let a bad wife find room to work"
**Issue:** ἐξουσίαν ἐκφέρεσθαι — "authority/permission to go out." LOGOS's "free rein" is an idiom that captures the meaning. PNEUMA's "find room to work" is loose. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "do not give a wicked wife free rein."

---

## Disagreement 014 — 25:26 "cut-her-off from your-flesh / cut her off"
**Verse:** 25:26
**EMET:** "cut-her-off from your-flesh"
**LOGOS:** "cut her off from your flesh"
**PNEUMA:** "cut her loose"
**Issue:** ἀπόκοψον αὐτὴν ἀπὸ τῶν σαρκῶν σου — "cut her off from your flesh." The "flesh" terminology echoes Gen 2:24 ("one flesh"). The cutting/divorce is explicitly a severing of the one-flesh union. PNEUMA loses this important allusion by omitting "flesh."
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "cut her off from your flesh" — the allusion to Genesis 2:24 must be preserved.
